fulltext: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，微软 Xbox 于当地时间 11 月 4 日宣布，为 Xbox Cloud Gaming 推出一项新功能，支持用户使用 iOS 或 Android 智能手机充当游戏手柄，在兼容智能电视上游玩云游戏时，无需额外连接实体手柄。
根据 Xbox 官方公告，该功能目前处于预览测试阶段，正在支持 Xbox Cloud Gaming 的国家和地区逐步推出。微软表示，用户可以通过手机浏览器加载虚拟游戏控制界面，无需额外下载手机应用。
使用时，用户需要在支持的智能电视上打开 Xbox 应用，进入「设置」中的「账户」，开启「预览功能」之后，在没有连接实体手柄的情况下启动游戏，电视屏幕便会显示使用手机作为控制器的选项。
用户选择该选项后，通过手机扫描电视显示的二维码，即可在手机浏览器中打开虚拟控制器界面。微软还表示，部分游戏将提供针对具体玩法定制的触控布局，以适应不同游戏的操作需求。
设备支持方面，这项功能适用于运行 Android 和 iOS 系统的手机，但微软暂未公布具体的系统版本要求；兼容的智能电视设备包括亚马逊 Fire TV Omni QLED 系列、运行 webOS 24 或更新版本的 LG 电视及显示器，以及搭载海信 VIDAA OS 9.6 或更新版本的电视。
IT之家注意到，微软还公布了 Xbox Nano Controller 的另一项测试功能 Cloud Connect。根据 Xbox 官方说明，该功能允许手柄通过 Wi-Fi 直连云服务器，而不是像传统方式那样通过蓝牙连接电视，再由电视转发。微软称，这种连接方式有望降低输入延迟，让游戏操作更加灵敏。
不过，Cloud Connect 目前仅面向美国用户开放预览，支持设备包括部分智能电视和网页端。用户需要通过 Android 版 Xbox Beta 应用或 PC 版 Xbox Accessories 应用完成手柄设置，其中通过 PC 应用设置还需要加入 Xbox Insider 计划。

fulltext: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据新华社今日报道，中国科学院空间应用工程与技术中心依托梦天舱超冷原子物理实验柜，利用全光阱冷却技术，将铷原子云的等效温度降至 9.7 皮开尔文，较室温降低 14 个数量级，并实现持续 7 秒的稳定观测，刷新了人类已知的最低温度纪录。
IT之家注：皮开尔文是极微小的温度单位，1 皮开尔文等于一万亿分之一开尔文（1 pK = 10⁻¹² K），而绝对零度（0 K，约零下 273.15 摄氏度）是热力学所允许的温度下限，只能无限接近而无法达到。
9.7 皮开尔文意味着铷原子云的温度仅比绝对零度高出一百亿分之一摄氏度左右。此前的纪录由德国科研团队于 2021 年创造，当时基于原子芯片磁阱方案将铷原子云冷却至 38 皮开尔文，自由膨胀时间约 2 秒。
中国团队的成果将这一数字压低至四分之一左右，观测窗口也延长至 7 秒，为捕捉极低温下的微弱物理信号提供了更充裕的时间。
此次实验在微重力环境下完成，这是突破地面极限的关键。在地面上，重力会使原子云迅速下坠，要维持悬浮就必须施加更强的束缚场，而束缚场本身会引入额外能量，反过来限制温度进一步下探，地面类似实验的稳定观测时间通常仅约 0.05 秒。空间站的微重力条件让原子云得以近乎自由地漂浮，仅需极弱的光学约束即可实现深度冷却。
中国团队选择的技术路线是全光阱冷却，区别于国际同行惯用的原子芯片磁阱方案。全光阱利用聚焦激光束构建势阱，对磁场干扰不敏感，并且适配后续的光晶格实验，扩展能力更强。

实验系统本身是一项高度集成的工程成果。地面实验装置原本占地约 20 立方米、重达 10 吨，科研人员将其压缩至 0.7 立方米、约 500 公斤，装入空间站实验柜中，涉及超高真空获取、高功率光纤激光器、精密光学对准等多环节的技术攻关。二十余束激光需要汇聚到直径仅几十微米的原子云上，对准误差控制在 5 微米以内，约为一根头发丝直径的十分之一，同时满足航天级高集成、低功耗与可靠性要求。该实验柜于 2022 年随梦天舱发射入轨，项目从论证到在轨取得成果历时约 15 年。
在接近绝对零度的条件下，铷原子云进入玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚态，原本无序热运动的原子呈现出宏观量子行为。
论文摘要显示，此次制备的凝聚体包含约 2.0×10⁴个原子，等效温度的不确定度范围为 9.7（+3.2/−2.7）皮开尔文，是首次在微重力环境下利用全光阱实现量子简并气体。更低的温度和更长的自由演化时间，为研究极低温量子气体的相变、非平衡动力学与多体关联等基础问题提供了地面难以复现的实验平台，也有助于推动早期宇宙模拟、超轻暗物质探测等前沿方向。
在应用层面，超冷原子可用于研制更高精度的原子干涉仪、量子传感器与空间时频基准，服务于重力场测量、惯性导航及基本物理常数检验。
相关论文《太空中低于 10 皮开尔文的量子气体》今日发表在国际学术期刊《科学》上。《科学》审稿人评价称，这项工作代表了超低温膨胀领域当前的最高水平。

cards.title: Samsung One UI 9.5 brings notable changes to Health and Calendar
cards.title_cn: Samsung One UI 9.5 为健康和日历带来显着变化
cards.summary: 【Android Authority】TL;DR Early One UI 9.5 test builds reveal upcoming changes to Samsung Calendar and Samsung Health. Samsung Calendar is getting a cleaner, grid-free interface, a relocated search button, and a new Key…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Samsung’s One UI 9 rollout is still underway, but that isn’t stopping the South Korean tech giant from preparing its next big software update. With One UI 9.5 currently in development, and an early beta build for the Galaxy S26 Ultra already spotted on a test server, we’re starting to inch closer to Samsung’s second Android 17-based update.
Samsung hasn’t detailed what’s coming with the update, but that hasn’t stopped testers from getting their hands on the unreleased software and uncovering the changes.
The latest discoveries shed light on two first-party apps: Samsung Health and Samsung Calendar, both of which appear to be getting some love with One UI 9.5, as highlighted by SamMobile.
The image on the left highlights what Google Calendar looks like with One UI 9, while the image on the right highlights what it could look like with One UI 9.5.

There are three main notable changes here. For starters, Samsung appears to have removed the individual rectangular backgrounds surrounding each date, so instead of appearing against a contrasting cell, dates now simply float against a black background. This makes the boundaries between dates much less obvious. At the same time, it gives the view a lot more room to breathe.

Secondly, the search button has been relocated from the top right of the view to the bottom right, sitting right next to the Add event pill. Speaking of which, the pill itself now surfaces less text. It only says “Add event” without referencing the currently selected date.

Elsewhere, the search screen now also appears to highlight a new Key events section, which reportedly displays important events as pill-shaped shortcuts. As seen in the second screenshot above, the section will appear above the existing calendar and color menus. And as seen in the last image above, the app’s sidebar is being reorganized too. The Sync now, Recycle bin, and Settings options now appear to have been relocated above the account list.

The updated Samsung Health offers some UI changes, but the bigger addition here is Mindful note, a new in-app journaling feature. The addition aims to offer Samsung users a safe place to reflect, note down thoughts, and “capture a moment, a feeling, or whatever comes to mind.”

You have the option to start with a blank slate or get some ideas with prompts, including About yourself, Relationships, Work and goals, and What if…? There’s also an option to set reminders, which should come in handy if you’re trying to make journaling a daily habit.
The changes mentioned above have only been spotted in prerelease software. These might never make it out widely, and if they do, they might or might not look and function as described here.

三星 One UI 9 的推出仍在进行中，但这并没有阻止这家韩国科技巨头准备下一次重大软件更新。目前 One UI 9.5 正在开发中，并且 Galaxy S26 Ultra 的早期 Beta 版本已经在测试服务器上发现，我们距离三星第二次基于 Android 17 的更新越来越近了。
三星尚未详细说明更新的内容，但这并没有阻止测试人员接触未发布的软件并发现变化。
最新发现揭示了两款第一方应用程序：三星健康和三星日历，正如 SamMobile 强调的那样，这两款应用程序似乎都受到 One UI 9.5 的青睐。

其次，搜索按钮已从视图的右上角移至右下角，位于“添加事件”药丸旁边。说到这里，药丸本身现在显示的文字更少了。它只说“添加事件”，而不引用当前选择的日期。

更新后的三星健康提供了一些用户界面更改，但更大的新增内容是 Mindful note，这是一项新的应用内日记功能。该功能旨在为三星用户提供一个安全的场所来反思、记下想法并“捕捉瞬间、感觉或任何想到的东西”。
您可以选择从白纸开始，也可以根据提示获得一些想法，包括关于您自己、人际关系、工作和目标以及如果……会怎样？还有一个设置提醒的选项，如果您想养成每天写日记的习惯，这应该会派上用场。
上述更改仅在预发行软件中发现。这些可能永远不会广泛传播，即使广泛传播，它们的外观和功能可能会也可能不会如本文所述。

cards.title: Google Forms will start using Gemini to summarize responses and uncover trends
cards.title_cn: Google Forms 将开始使用 Gemini 来总结回复并发现趋势
cards.summary: 【Google】Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google is introducing actionable insights to Google Forms. The new feature uses Gemini to analyze the form responses, uncover trends, and recommend next s…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Get ready for an injection of Gemini into your Google Forms. The Mountain View-based firm has announced that it is rolling out an update for the platform. This update will introduce actionable insights that you’ll be able to access straight from the Responses tab of your form.

According to the announcement, these actionable insights use Gemini to analyze responses, uncover trends, and recommend next steps. With its ability to spot patterns, the AI is able to reveal how answers connect. And what’s an AI tool without summarization capabilities? Google says the tool will give you an overview of the key takeaways.

For example, if you create a registration-focused form, the tool will let you know who’s signing up. Or if you created a form for event feedback, the insights will let you know what respondents valued most.

The gradual rollout of actionable insights in Google Forms has started. It will be available to Google AI Pro and Ultra customers. Business, Enterprise, and Education customers are also getting access. Google warns that it could take up to 15 days for visibility.

fulltext: Share This Article
AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action.
Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task.
As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power.

What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt.

Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity.
The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU.

cards.title: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
cards.title_cn: 用于交互式世界模拟的全新 NVIDIA Cosmos 3 开放模型
cards.summary: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
fulltext: NVIDIA Cosmos world model development platform adds four new open-weight checkpoints to its Cosmos 3 model family for generating interactive world simulation and multi-sensor multi-view driving scenes:
All four models are post-trained examples of Cosmos 3 Nano and have 16B trainable parameters. The models use OpenMDW1.1, permitting commercial and non-commercial use under its terms.
Download the checkpoints · Read the technical report . Watch the demos

🦾 Robotics needs environments that can answer this across changing scenes and viewpoints. These checkpoints offer complementary ways to build them: Sim-Bimanual predicts visual consequences from actions, while Sim-Transfer turns a physics simulator’s controls into generated observations.

🚦 For autonomous driving, appearance and geometry must agree. Synchronized camera and LiDAR generation connects visual observations with 3D sensing. Scene and traffic-signal controls let researchers vary road layouts and signal states, then study how a driving policy responds.

🔄 Each observation can shape the next action. Streaming generation connects video prediction to ongoing interaction, giving world-model researchers a way to explore how actions and observations unfold together.

🌐 An open foundation for others to build on. NVIDIA’s vision is to help researchers and developers create richer, more responsive simulated worlds. Open weights and post-training recipes provide a shared starting point for adapting models, comparing methods, and contributing improvements. These problems remain hard: the work ahead is to measure where the models faithfully support policy learning and evaluation, understand their limits, and improve where they fall short.

Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto is a bidirectional model for offline synthetic driving data generation. It generates synchronized video across up to 11 camera views, including fisheyes, and supports joint RGB–LiDAR generation. Per-camera World Scenario Map (WSM) controls specify scene structure and traffic motion, while text prompts guide appearance.

Developers can vary environmental conditions to expand training and evaluation coverage, with optional initial RGB images to anchor scene appearance. Joint LiDAR generation additionally uses aligned HD-map range-map controls. Transfer-Auto also serves as the foundation for adapting Cosmos to your own sensor rig and driving domain. Start by post-training it on your data to accommodate your camera layout, LiDAR configuration, and target environment. The adapted model can be used directly for offline data generation or undergo causal training and few-step distillation for fast streaming simulation—the development path used to create Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto.

Prefer a notebook? Open Transfer-Auto.

Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto is the causally distilled streaming variant of Transfer-Auto. It generates successive small chunks of synchronized camera video and LiDAR in just a few denoising steps, using generated history and updated driving controls to support fast streaming and long, interactive rollouts.

Provide per-camera captions and synchronized WSM controls, optionally adding initial RGB images. For LiDAR generation, include HD-Map range controls aligned with the camera controls. The distilled model generates successive chunks using its rolling history. Closed-loop interaction requires a simulation runtime and WSM renderer to update those controls from driving inputs. For a new sensor rig or domain, adapt Transfer-Auto first, then distill it into Sim-Auto.
Point your agent to the open skill : Run inference with Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto
Prefer a notebook? Open Sim-Auto.
Your simulator computes motion, contacts, and physical state. Sim-Transfer uses its spatial controls and a text prompt to render color observations that a policy can consume.
Action → simulator update → spatial controls → generated RGB → next policy action
Depth: relative distance from the camera.
Segmentation: regions and object boundaries.
Edges: scene contours.
Blur: coarse appearance and layout.
Text guides appearance; physics and ground-truth state stay with the simulator.
Depth control to video
Segmentation control to video
Point your agent to the open skill : Run inference with Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer
Prefer a notebook? Use Transfer.
Input Frames
Output Video From Sim-Bimanual Simulation Checkpoint

Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual simulates how an environment evolves in response to a bimanual robot’s actions. It supports interactive two-arm simulation for YAM and AgiBot embodiments, controlled by a policy or human-operated joysticks.
Start with an image, move the robot or camera, and generate the next observations. One control sequence can switch between viewpoint changes and manipulation.

The mixed-action example uses 59 control values, padded to 64 during training. Its schema defines coordinate frames, rotations, gripper calibration, validity masks, and control domains. Follow those conventions so each value describes the intended motion.
Keep timing aligned: T transitions need T+1 observations. Training transforms raw captures into the model’s action representation; released inference actions are already normalized.
Here, Sim-Transfer generates visuals from a physics simulator’s updated state; Sim-Bimanual generates the next observation directly from the scene and robot actions.
See the data contract and action schema.

Requirements: Linux, an NVIDIA GPU, Docker, and NVIDIA Container Toolkit. The published vLLM-Omni setup was tested on one GB200; this is not a minimum-memory specification. The server downloads weights; the clients fetch sample inputs.
Point your agent to the open skill : Run inference with Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual
Prefer a notebook? Open Bimanual

Cosmos 3’s Mixture-of-Transformers backbone connects separate text-processing and visual-generation networks through attention. The generator predicts each short segment from the prompt, available controls, and generated history.
Controls + history → generate chunk → decode images → update history

Denoising refines noisy, compressed video representations into a segment. Temporal-causal attention lets it read available history and controls while blocking future target observations. A key/value cache retains attention information for the next prediction.

The model operates on compressed video representations called latents. After the initial image, each latent time step represents four RGB frames. Transfer predicts one step per chunk; the optimized Bimanual setup in the report predicts two. Smaller chunks let new controls affect generation more often.
Stage 0 — Bidirectional adaptation: learn the domain and its control-to-video relationships from complete recorded clips.
Stage 1 — Teacher forcing: predict each chunk from earlier recorded observations and available controls, with the clean answer and future targets masked out.
Stage 2 — Consistency distillation: use a frozen teacher to train a student that generates each chunk in four denoising steps.
Stage 3 — Self-forcing: train on the student’s generated history. A frozen teacher and an auxiliary score model supply the distribution-matching signal.

Why the final stage matters: a slightly mispredicted object becomes context for later frames, so errors can compound. Self-forcing exposes training to that generated history. Distillation and caching reduce the cost of producing each observation.

The post-training recipes start from Cosmos3-Nano or compatible base weights and cover all four stages. Keep full training checkpoints to resume; exported inference weights omit optimizer and other training state.
Transfer-auto: Post-train on your driving data to adapt to your sensor rig and domain, and generate offline synthetic data.
Sim-auto: Apply causal training and distillation to an adapted Transfer-Auto model for fast streaming simulation.
Sim-Transfer : Post-train the checkpoint for your environment with local data preparation, stage configurations, and resume.
Sim-Bimanual: Post-train for your embodiment with data validation, stage configurations, checkpoint handoffs, and export.

该模型对称为潜在特征的压缩视频表示进行操作。在初始图像之后，每个潜在时间步代表四个 RGB 帧。 Transfer 预测每个块的一个步骤；报告中优化的双手设置预测有两个。较小的块让新控件更频繁地影响生成。
第 0 阶段 — 双向适应：从完整录制的剪辑中学习领域及其控制与视频的关系。
第一阶段——教师强迫：根据早期记录的观察结果和可用的控制来预测每个块，并掩盖清晰的答案和未来的目标。
第 2 阶段 - 一致性蒸馏：使用冻结的教师来训练学生，使其通过四个去噪步骤生成每个块。
第三阶段——自我强迫：训练学生生成的历史。冻结的教师和辅助评分模型提供分布匹配信号。

Sim-Transfer：通过本地数据准备、阶段配置和恢复对您的环境进行后训练检查点。
Sim-Bimanual：通过数据验证、阶段配置、检查点切换和导出对您的实施例进行后期训练。
为您的编码代理提供技能和数据集位置。遵循环境检查、验证样本、测试训练并在长时间运行之前重新启动。评估持续事件的质量：成功的短期运行验证执行，而不是收敛。

cards.summary: 【Android Authority】TL;DR Samsung Android XR smart glasses are nearly here, with pre-orders now confirmed to open on November 12. The audio-based smart glasses, developed in collaboration with Google, will feature frames…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Smart glasses are about to enter quite possibly their biggest era yet, with the release of Google and Samsung’s new Android XR collaboration, and now we finally know when you can get your order in. The companies have been teasing these wearables for months now, featuring frames from the likes of Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Last month we heard that a November launch was supposedly confirmed, and today pre-order details are starting to go official.
There’s not much to share just yet, but we do have a date: Pre-orders for Samsung’s “Intelligent Eyewear” open in one week, on November 12.

We’ve already seen the frames, and we know to expect an audio-first Android XR experience — Samsung models with integrated displays will have to wait. Recent rumors have suggested that the glasses will ultimately ship sometime in December, which would neatly fit with this pre-order window.

With any luck, next week’s opening of pre-orders will not just confirm that release date, but also finally reveal exactly what Samsung has in mind for pricing. That’s arguably the biggest outstanding question that’s been hanging over this launch. You won’t be paying anything like the $1,800 the bulky Samsung Galaxy XR headset runs, but these could still end up costing you as much as a decent phone.

Shoppers securing their pre-orders can look forward to using the smart glasses for help navigating around town, assisting with translations, or just chatting with Gemini to get information about whatever’s on their mind. They’re also equipped with cameras for recoding spontaneous moments — and yes, Samsung is taking all the expected privacy-preserving steps like lighting up an LED while recording and refusing to film if it detects the LED has been covered.

For as excited as we are to see these glasses finally land, it also probably couldn’t be happening at a worse time. Governments around the world are pushing back against smart glasses, limiting just how and where users are able to operate them. Ideally, regulators and manufacturers will eventually be able to meet in the middle with some mutually satisfactory compromise, but we’ll have to wait and see what shape that might take.

cards.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
cards.title_cn: 走进全方位：开发人员如何利用前沿人工智能代理将想法转化为模拟
cards.summary: 【NVIDIA】Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI mo…
fulltext: Share This Article
Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead.

Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs.
Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities.
Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem.

Creating animated 3D content requires connecting modeling, simulation, materials and rendering. Nick Scarcella, a senior technical artist on NVIDIA’s BondLab team, directed AI agents — primarily using Claude — to work with CUDA libraries and Isaac Sim to create animations. The BondLab team uses SideFX Houdini and the NVIDIA ovrtx library to develop materials, lighting and the final rendered appearance.

In one experiment, Scarcella guided Astra to recreate an OP-1 portable synthesizer using product images, manuals and technical direction. He exported the model into the OpenUSD framework, tested it in Houdini and Blender, then used Astra and Opus to refine details before adjusting materials and textures for ovrtx rendering.

Scarcella also used a publicly shared robot-hand checkpoint in Isaac Sim, directing the motion and developing materials and lighting in Houdini with Claude’s assistance. Working with team member Steven Dvornik, the team created an “Echos” visualization: translucent versions of the hand overlap and merge into a single hand animation, offering a visual interpretation of robot training.
Figure: An artistic visualization of simulated robot-hand motion, developed with AI assistance and Houdini’s materials and lighting tools.
These workflows bring agent-assisted creation into existing artist tools, giving teams editable content they can inspect, refine and render across applications.
Explore Scarcella’s Houdini MCP tools and agent skill.

Before a robot can disassemble a product, developers need to know whether its tools can reach and remove the parts. Jens Jebens, a senior product manager for OpenUSD at NVIDIA, directed Astra to model a car suspension in PTC Onshape and configure it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
Jebens used simulation feedback to revise the tooling, including a wrench designed to reach the suspension’s bolts, and reported successful removal of a suspension component in simulation.

PTC also connects computer-aided design (CAD) with simulation through Onshape’s SimReady Publisher, built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Robotics startup Sensori uses it to transfer its Yuri robot into Isaac Sim, carrying geometry, joints and configuration data so the team can evaluate design changes without repeatedly rebuilding the simulation model.
Read Sensori’s story.
Explore the Onshape importer guide.

Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation.

David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes.

Wehr guided Astra to interpret panoramic photos, create building geometry and align it with point-cloud measurements. OpenUSD stores the models, while Omniverse’s ovrtx library renders results for inspection.
Explore NVIDIA Omniverse agent skills to help agents build with Omniverse libraries.

Before changing how industrial equipment operates, engineers need a way to explore the consequences. Pradeep Kaushik, a member of the NVIDIA Omniverse developer relations team, directed Astra to build a what-if analysis application around a simulated gas turbine and generator.

The application lets users adjust conditions such as load, ambient temperature and fuel composition, then compare power, efficiency, fuel consumption and equipment response. Six test procedures explore scenarios including load changes, a stuck fuel valve and an exhaust-sensor error.
The prototype gives engineers an interactive way to investigate how operating changes and faults could affect equipment behavior, supporting decisions about which scenarios warrant further testing.

Astra used tools like Cantera for thermochemistry and SciPy for equipment dynamics. The application maps solver results to rotor animation and color-coded temperature, pressure and flow-velocity indicators in a 3D turbine. NVIDIA Omniverse libraries update the scene (ovstage), render it with RTX (ovrtx) and stream the view to the browser (ovstream). Engineers can rotate and zoom the cutaway, switch between indicators, and pause or scrub through a simulated response alongside charts and virtual instruments.

With SimReady Central Library, announced at GTC Berlin, developers can access more than 2,000 simulation-ready USD assets from equipment manufacturers and asset providers for robotics simulations and AI factory digital twins workflows.

Paul Kind, a member of NVIDIA’s Omniverse documentation team, pointed an AI agent to the library and guided scene assembly through conversation. His kitchen scene included 180 placements drawn from 63 unique library assets, alongside 18 custom geometry pieces. Kind reviewed renders produced with Isaac Sim and guided further adjustments.
For robotics and factory workflows, developers can select SimReady assets with the simulation properties embedded to fit their required task then test in an assembled environment.
Find assets in SimReady Central Library, and learn how to contribute.
A warehouse simulation needs to keep running smoothly as more robot arms, conveyors and boxes fill the scene.

When it slows down, developers need to identify what’s holding it back. Bhavik Sanganee, principal engineer at NVIDIA, used Astra with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build a warehouse simulation, increase its complexity and investigate slowdowns.

Performance first fell below the target when the scene doubled in size. Running physics calculations, image rendering and video preparation concurrently restored performance and enabled further scaling.
With 80 conveyors, 40 arms and 800 boxes, the simulation sustained 30 frames per second at full HD resolution during a two-minute test. The arms completed 640 successful box placements.
Doubling the scene again reduced performance. Testing traced the slowdown to the physics and robot-control pipeline, giving Sanganee a specific area to improve.
Start building with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries.

In electronics assembly, a robot may need to position a flexible cable around components before plugging it into a port. The cable bends as the robot moves it, and the connector must line up precisely to fit.

Oyindamola Omotuyi, robotics technical marketing manager at NVIDIA, directed Astra to build a robot simulation using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Newton physics and Omniverse rendering with a Robotiq gripper handling the cable.

Astra also developed a reinforcement learning system that combined learned cable-routing movements with position-and-orientation feedback and corrective adjustments for USB-C insertion. The simulation gave Omotuyi a way to test cable handling and connector alignment before moving to physical-robot experiments.
The controller used information supplied directly by the simulation. Next steps include testing a friction-held grasp and using information a physical robot could obtain from cameras and sensors.
Get started with robot learning in NVIDIA Isaac Lab.

Before testing whether a robot can pick up and move a box, developers need a simulation model with joints that move correctly and with grippers that can hold the object. A computer-aided design (CAD) model provides the robot’s shape, but it still needs physics properties to perform the task.

Using an ABB Robotics YuMi robot, developers directed Astra with NVIDIA Omniverse content libraries to convert CAD files into OpenUSD, match the robot’s appearance to reference images, and configure joints and collision geometry. They checked the asset against SimReady Foundation requirements before testing it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

Both arms and grippers completed four cube pick-and-place cycles, using simulated finger contact and friction. These tests demonstrated behavior under the simulated conditions — estimated physical properties were not calibrated against the real robot.
Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view.

Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views.

DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics (ovphysx), scene updates (ovstage), rendering (ovrtx) and the user interface (ovui). He also used Astra with SimReady (simready-foundation) to create the physical scene in simulation. Astra then generated animation and application code to bring those capabilities together.
Learn how to prepare and validate SimReady robot assets with frontier AI models and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries.

Changing a scene, sensor or driving model can significantly affect autonomous-vehicle simulations. Doyub Kim, a manager on the simulation technology team at NVIDIA, asked Astra to build Zero to Alpamayo — a reusable simulation environment based on San Francisco’s Market Street.

Kim directed Astra to map out the workflow, then connect asset creation, traffic, Omniverse RTX sensor simulation and Alpamayo driving in stages, checking each integration. The resulting prototype was a testing ground for comparing models and tracing how scene or sensor changes affect downstream driving behavior. A separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varied weather and lighting in recorded simulation videos, allowing Kim to compare the driving model’s responses to the same scenario under different conditions.
Comparing recorded and simulated camera and lidar outputs gives developers key performance indicator-based feedback for refining a scene.

To test robots and autonomous vehicles, developers need to know how closely simulated sensors match real ones. Ashley Reid, who works on RTX sensor validation at NVIDIA, directed Astra and Claude Fable 5 agents to compare ovrtx camera and raw LiDAR outputs with recorded data. The agents created two digital twins from scratch and improved two existing ones. Over about three days, Reid guided an iterative workflow in which agents measured differences, created or modified OpenUSD scenes, and checked the results. Changes addressed missing objects, geometry and materials, with acceptance depending on camera and LiDAR metrics. This gives developers a way to use measured discrepancies to guide scene creation and improvement.
Start by rendering an OpenUSD scene with the ovrtx minimal Python example, then define a sensor measure to compare with recorded data.

Teaching robots new movements means checking whether those actions work under physical constraints. Tae Kim, who leads NVIDIA Omniverse engineering and product, used sports videos and natural-language instructions to guide Astra in building Robo Olympics, an experimental project that tests simulated Unitree G1 humanoids performing sports movements.

Under Kim’s direction, Astra built controllers and refined them through physics trials. Newton Physics Engine simulated behavior, the open source NVIDIA Warp framework accelerated calculations and ovrtx rendered scenes and virtual-camera images. In one experiment, the robot cleared a single hurdle in 64 of 100 simulation trials. The trials gave Kim feedback for improving the robot’s timing and control.
Watch Kim explore building simulations with Astra and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries.

Turning 3D models into an application requires connecting assets, live data and an interface. Nic Johns, an engineering director at NVIDIA, prompted Astra to assemble NASA assets into an OpenUSD International Space Station model with telemetry. Johns built the application with a single prompt, then used a follow-up prompt to shift the scene to Earth’s daytime side so the planet was visible.

The workflow used Blender for asset preparation and Omniverse libraries for rendering (ovrtx), scene runtime (ovstage) and streaming (ovstream). The application brings 3D models and operational data into the browser, with Johns guiding its development through prompts and corrections.
Try the Omniverse Real-Time Viewer skill.

A digitally reconstructed room needs editable objects and accurate physical behavior before developers can test interactions. Chirag Majithia, from the Isaac engineering applications team at NVIDIA, directed Astra to turn stereo camera captures into an editable OpenUSD studio.

The workflow combined PyCuSFM, FoundationStereo and nvblox for reconstruction, with user review guiding object selection and placement. Astra assembled generated and Blender-authored assets and used USD Content Agents to configure how objects move and interact in simulation. Isaac Sim tests guided collision and contact revisions for doors and drawers. The studio connects captured geometry to interaction testing, making gaps and object behavior easier to inspect.
Explore USD Content Agents.
Have a simulation idea? Explore NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to start building with an AI agent.
Wednesday, Oct. 21 11 a.m.-1 p.m. CEST
cards.summary_cn: 【NVIDIA】将模拟想法转变为可行的应用程序意味着组装资源、连接物理和渲染，并检查场景是否按预期运行。开发人员正在结合前沿人工智能模块……
fulltext_cn: 分享这篇文章
您的浏览器不支持 HTML5 视频。这是视频的链接。
将模拟想法转变为可行的应用程序意味着组装资源、连接物理和渲染，并检查场景是否按预期运行。开发人员正在将前沿 AI 模型与 NVIDIA Omniverse 库相结合，以帮助完成这项工作——构建用于探索场景、调查故障和改进设计的应用程序。
开发人员通过自然语言指令指导人工智能代理、审查结果并指导更改。 Omniverse 库提供 GPU 加速的物理、渲染和传感器模拟功能。
探索以下项目，了解 GPT-6 Astra 等前沿 AI 模型的实际应用，并查看整个生态系统中 NVIDIA 团队和开发人员提供的新示例。
创建动画 3D 内容需要连接建模、模拟、材质和渲染。 NVIDIA BondLab 团队的高级技术艺术家 Nick Scarcella 指导 AI 代理（主要使用 Claude）与 CUDA 库和 Isaac Sim 合作来创建动画。 BondLab 团队使用 SideFX Houdini 和 NVIDIA ovrtx 库来开发材质、照明和最终渲染外观。
在一项实验中，Scarcella 指导 Astra 使用产品图像、手册和技术指导重新创建了 OP-1 便携式合成器。他将模型导出到 OpenUSD 框架中，在 Houdini 和 Blender 中进行测试，然后使用 Astra 和 Opus 细化细节，然后调整 ovrtx 渲染的材质和纹理。
斯卡塞拉还在 Isaac Sim 中使用了一个公开共享的机器人手检查点，在克劳德的协助下指导胡迪尼的运动并开发材料和照明。该团队与团队成员 Steven Dvornik 合作，创建了“Echos”可视化：半透明版本的手重叠并合并成单手动画，提供机器人训练的视觉解释。
图：利用 AI 辅助以及 Houdini 的材质和照明工具开发的模拟机器人手运动的艺术可视化。
这些工作流程将代理辅助创作引入现有的艺术家工具中，为团队提供可编辑的内容，他们可以跨应用程序检查、优化和渲染。
探索 Scarcella 的 Houdini MCP 工具和代理技能。
在机器人拆卸产品之前，开发人员需要知道其工具是否可以到达并拆卸零件。 NVIDIA OpenUSD 高级产品经理 Jens Jebens 指示 Astra 在 PTC Onshape 中对汽车悬架进行建模，并在 NVIDIA Isaac Sim 中对其进行配置。
Jebens 使用模拟反馈来修改工具，包括设计用于触及悬架螺栓的扳手，并报告在模拟中成功拆卸了悬架部件。
PTC 还通过 Onshape 的 SimReady Publisher（使用 NVIDIA Omniverse 库构建）将计算机辅助设计 (CAD) 与仿真连接起来。机器人初创公司 Sensori 使用它将其 Yuri 机器人转移到 Isaac Sim 中，携带几何结构、关节和配置数据，以便团队可以评估设计变更，而无需重复重建仿真模型。
阅读 Sensori 的故事。
探索 Onshape 导入器指南。
规划仓库自动化需要建筑物本身的模型，但货架和机械可能会在现场扫描中掩盖其结构。 Omniverse 汇集了真实到模拟工具和代理技能，帮助开发人员将现实世界的捕获转化为物理 AI 模拟的可编辑起始环境。
NVIDIA 模拟技术团队的 David Wehr 在这项工作的基础上，使用 Astra 开发了一个工作流程，可以在没有内容的情况下以数字方式重建建筑物。目标是建立一个可编辑、可模拟的建筑模型，开发人员可以在其中添加或重新定位货架和机械，以在进行物理更改之前评估仓库布局和自动化计划。
Wehr 指导 Astra 解读全景照片、创建建筑几何形状并将其与点云测量值对齐。 OpenUSD 存储模型，而 Omniverse 的 ovrtx 库则呈现结果以供检查。
探索 NVIDIA Omniverse 代理技能，帮助代理使用 Omniverse 库进行构建。
在改变工业设备的运行方式之前，工程师需要一种方法来探索其后果。 NVIDIA Omniverse 开发者关系团队成员 Pradeep Kaushik 指导 Astra 围绕模拟燃气轮机和发电机构建假设分析应用程序。
该应用程序允许用户调整负载、环境温度和燃料成分等条件，然后比较功率、效率、燃料消耗和设备响应。六个测试程序探讨了负载变化、燃油阀卡住和排气传感器错误等场景。
该原型为工程师提供了一种交互式方式来调查操作变化和故障如何影响设备行为，支持有关哪些场景需要进一步测试的决策。

Astra 使用 Cantera 等工具进行热化学分析，使用 SciPy 进行设备动力学分析。该应用程序将求解器结果映射到 3D 涡轮机中的转子动画和颜色编码的温度、压力和流速指示器。 NVIDIA Omniverse 库更新场景 (ovstage)，使用 RTX (ovrtx) 进行渲染，并将视图流式传输到浏览器 (ovstream)。工程师可以旋转和缩放剖面图、在指标之间切换、暂停或清理模拟响应以及图表和虚拟仪器。
借助柏林 GTC 上宣布的 SimReady Central Library，开发人员可以访问来自设备制造商和资产提供商的 2,000 多种模拟就绪美元资产，用于机器人模拟和 AI 工厂数字孪生工作流程。
NVIDIA Omniverse 文档团队成员 Paul Kind 将 AI 代理指向该库，并通过对话指导场景组装。他的厨房场景包括从 63 个独特的库资源中提取的 180 个位置，以及 18 个自定义几何图形。对 Isaac Sim 制作的渲染进行了亲切的审查并指导进一步的调整。
对于机器人和工厂工作流程，开发人员可以选择嵌入了模拟属性的 SimReady 资产来满足其所需的任务，然后在组装环境中进行测试。
在 SimReady Central Library 中查找资产，并了解如何做出贡献。
随着越来越多的机器人手臂、传送带和箱子填满场景，仓库模拟需要保持平稳运行。
当速度变慢时，开发人员需要找出阻碍其发展的因素。 NVIDIA 首席工程师 Bhavik Sanganee 使用 Astra 和 NVIDIA Omniverse 库来构建仓库模拟，增加其复杂性并调查减速情况。
当场景尺寸增加一倍时，性能首先低于目标。同时运行物理计算、图像渲染和视频准备可恢复性能并实现进一步扩展。
该模拟使用 80 个传送带、40 个臂和 800 个箱子，在两分钟的测试中以全高清分辨率维持每秒 30 帧的速度。手臂完成了 640 次成功的盒子放置。
将场景加倍又降低了性能。测试将速度放缓追溯到物理和机器人控制管道，这给了 Sanganee 一个需要改进的特定领域。
开始使用 NVIDIA Omniverse 库进行构建。
在电子组装中，机器人可能需要在将柔性电缆插入端口之前将其放置在组件周围。当机器人移动时，电缆会弯曲，连接器必须精确对齐才能安装。
NVIDIA 机器人技术营销经理 Oyindamola Omotuyi 指示 Astra 使用 NVIDIA Isaac Lab、牛顿物理和 Omniverse 渲染以及处理电缆的 Robotiq 夹具构建机器人模拟。
Astra 还开发了一种强化学习系统，该系统将学习的电缆布线运动与位置和方向反馈以及 USB-C 插入的校正调整相结合。该模拟为 Omotuyi 提供了一种在进行物理机器人实验之前测试电缆处理和连接器对齐的方法。
控制器使用由模拟直接提供的信息。接下来的步骤包括测试摩擦握持并使用物理机器人可以从摄像头和传感器获得的信息。
开始在 NVIDIA Isaac Lab 中进行机器人学习。
在测试机器人是否可以拾取并移动盒子之前，开发人员需要一个具有可正确移动的关节和可握住物体的夹具的仿真模型。计算机辅助设计（CAD）模型提供了机器人的形状，但它仍然需要物理属性来执行任务。
使用 ABB Robotics YuMi 机器人，开发人员利用 NVIDIA Omniverse 内容库指导 Astra 将 CAD 文件转换为 OpenUSD，将机器人的外观与参考图像进行匹配，并配置关节和碰撞几何形状。他们在 NVIDIA Isaac Sim 中进行测试之前，根据 SimReady Foundation 的要求检查了该资产。
使用模拟手指接触和摩擦，手臂和夹具完成了四个立方体拾取和放置循环。这些测试展示了模拟条件下的行为——估计的物理特性没有针对真实的机器人进行校准。
以第一人称和第三人称视角探索人形机器人的游戏化、基于物理的控制。
在自动化仓库任务之前，开发人员需要一个交互式模拟环境来探索任务行为并评估工作的完成方式。 NVIDIA Omniverse 产品经理 Frank DeLise 使用 Astra 将 SimReady 仓库和人形机器人转变为具有第一人称和第三人称视角的交互式模拟器。
DeLise 指示 Astra 连接 NVIDIA Omniverse 物理库 (ovphysx)、场景更新 (ovstage)、渲染 (ovrtx) 和用户界面 (ovui)。他还使用 Astra 和 SimReady (simready-foundation) 来创建模拟中的物理场景。然后，Astra 生成动画和应用程序代码，将这些功能整合在一起。
了解如何使用前沿 AI 模型和 NVIDIA Omniverse 库准备和验证 SimReady 机器人资产。
改变场景、传感器或驾驶模型会显着影响自动驾驶汽车的模拟。 NVIDIA 模拟技术团队经理 Doyub Kim 要求 Astra 构建 Zero to Alpamayo——一个基于旧金山市场街的可重复使用的模拟环境。
Kim 指导 Astra 制定工作流程，然后分阶段连接资产创建、流量、Omniverse RTX 传感器模拟和 Alpamayo 驾驶，检查每个集成。由此产生的原型是比较模型和追踪场景或传感器变化如何影响下游驾驶行为的试验场。一项单独的 Cosmos3-Nano 实验在录制的模拟视频中改变了天气和照明，使 Kim 能够比较驾驶模型在不同条件下对相同场景的响应。
比较记录和模拟的摄像机和激光雷达输出，为开发人员提供基于关键性能指标的反馈，以改进场景。

为了测试机器人和自动驾驶汽车，开发人员需要知道模拟传感器与真实传感器的匹配程度。在 NVIDIA 从事 RTX 传感器验证工作的 Ashley Reid 指示 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5 代理将 ovrtx 相机和原始 LiDAR 输出与记录的数据进行比较。特工们从头开始创建了两个数字双胞胎，并改进了两个现有的数字双胞胎。在大约三天的时间内，Reid 指导了一个迭代工作流程，其中代理测量差异、创建或修改 OpenUSD 场景并检查结果。更改解决了丢失的物体、几何形状和材料的问题，接受程度取决于相机和激光雷达指标。这为开发人员提供了一种使用测量的差异来指导场景创建和改进的方法。
首先使用 ovrtx 最小 Python 示例渲染 OpenUSD 场景，然后定义传感器测量以与记录的数据进行比较。
教机器人新的动作意味着检查这些动作在物理限制下是否有效。领导 NVIDIA Omniverse 工程和产品的 Tae Kim 使用体育视频和自然语言指令来指导 Astra 构建 Robo Olympics，这是一个测试模拟 Unitree G1 类人机器人执行体育运动的实验项目。
在 Kim 的指导下，Astra 制造了控制器并通过物理试验对其进行了改进。牛顿物理引擎模拟行为，开源 NVIDIA Warp 框架加速计算以及 ovrtx 渲染场景和虚拟相机图像。在一项实验中，机器人在 100 次模拟试验中的 64 次中清除了一个障碍。这些试验为 Kim 提供了改进机器人计时和控制的反馈。
观看 Kim 探索使用 Astra 和 NVIDIA Omniverse 库构建模拟。
将 3D 模型转变为应用程序需要连接资产、实时数据和接口。 NVIDIA 工程总监 Nic Johns 促使 Astra 将 NASA 的资产组装到具有遥测功能的 OpenUSD 国际空间站模型中。约翰斯使用单个提示构建了该应用程序，然后使用后续提示将场景转移到地球的白天一侧，以便可以看到地球。
该工作流程使用 Blender 进行资源准备，并使用 Omniverse 库进行渲染 (ovrtx)、场景运行时 (ovstage) 和流媒体 (ovstream)。该应用程序将 3D 模型和操作数据带入浏览器，约翰斯通过提示和更正指导其开发。
尝试 Omniverse 实时查看器技能。
在开发人员测试交互之前，数字重建的房间需要可编辑的对象和准确的物理行为。 NVIDIA Isaac 工程应用团队的 Chirag Majithia 指导 Astra 将立体相机捕获的图像转变成可编辑的 OpenUSD 工作室。
该工作流程结合了 PyCuSFM、FoundationStereo 和 nvblox 进行重建，并通过用户审查指导对象选择和放置。 Astra 组装了生成的和 Blender 创作的资源，并使用 USD 内容代理来配置对象在模拟中移动和交互的方式。 Isaac Sim 测试了门和抽屉的引导碰撞和接触修正。该工作室将捕获的几何图形与交互测试连接起来，使间隙和对象行为更容易检查。
探索美元内容代理。
有模拟想法吗？探索 NVIDIA Omniverse 库，开始使用 AI 代理进行构建。

cards.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
cards.title_cn: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash：快速、经济高效，具有更长的剪辑
cards.summary: 【Google】Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash brings native 15-second video generation and editing, stronger consistency, and 30% lower pricing.
fulltext: Today, we’re rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, and making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash introduces native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing capabilities, and enhanced reference following. We have dropped the price 30% from Gemini Omni 1.1 making it available at $0.07 per second for 720p video.
Here’s an overview of what’s new:

Beyond the lower price, the workflow keeps costs down: you can draft fast at 360p or 720p, fix a detail with a follow-up edit instead of re-generating the entire clip, and then upscale your best creations to 1080p or 4K.

You can now generate and edit videos natively up to 15 seconds long, up from 10 seconds with Omni 1.1. You can also specify duration in one-second increments from 3 to 15 seconds, giving you room to tell complete stories, create product explainers, or produce full social ad spots in a single generation.

You can guide generation combining character, product, or style images, short motion clips (up to three seconds), and audio cues — and Omni 1.2 Flash holds onto those details from start to finish. Faces, garments, packaging typography, and brand colors stay consistent across camera angles, making it easy to turn existing product photography or character sheets into virtual try-on clips, catalog spins, and branded video ads.

It feels like AI is cracking a new math problem every week. Last month, OpenAI released 719 manuscriptsclaiming solutions to some of the field’s hardest problems. But even the computer checks meant to confirm those results can slip. After years of AI slop, it’s fair to wonder whether math is next.

Axiom Math is betting math can avoid that fate, not by slowing down, but by standing on firmer ground. The $1.6 billion startup wants to build a verified foundation that AI agents can rely on to write software and, eventually, do science.

On Wednesday, the company announced it had formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the largest bodies of mathematics ever written by humans. Mathematicians often hold Stacks in rare regard — Columbia mathematician Peter Woit has claimed there’s “nothing else really comparable,” comparing the project to “the famous Bourbaki books,” a series that rebuilt math from its foundations in the 20th century.

Woit’s Columbia colleague Johan de Jong started the Stacks Project in 2005 as an open source reference. Mathematicians have contributed to it ever since, building out results from college-level algebra all the way up to the field’s most advanced ideas across algebra, geometry, and number theory.
The company’s fleet of AI agents translates the library’s roughly 7,654 pages into about 16 million lines of computer-checked code.

Formalizing math is a way of making sure the structure underneath it is sound. Mathematicians rewrite the proof as code in a programming language called Lean, and a program called a proof assistant checks the code line by line. If the proof passes, mathematicians can trust that it’s logically sound.
Engineers use the same idea, called formal verification, to confirm their chip designs work, while researchers in France have used it to catch bugs in software that calculates family benefits.

For a library like the Stacks Project, checking each theorem is only part of the job. The theorems and definitions in Stacks are interconnected, and each one builds on the ones before it. Like a family tree, many results in Stacks trace back to the ones that came before it.
That interconnectedness made Axiom unsure the project would work at first. The team had to keep every connection intact across about 16 million lines of Lean code.

“Things that are big and things that are delicate in life just don’t go together,” Axiom CEO Carina Hong told TechCrunch. “[Stacks] is a collection of mathematical results that is the foundation of mathematics. You want [theorems] to be consistent and not, like, paradoxical. You want the definitions to not fight with each other.”
The 25-year-old CEO dropped out of a Stanford math PhD program and founded the company in March 2025. In March, Axiom raised a $200 million Series A led by Menlo Ventures.
“We were not sure if vibe coding would be able to preserve the beauty of Stacks,” Hong said.

To pull off the project, the team gave its agents a loose structure and let them run in parallel. “With Stacks, we imposed a hierarchy … [but] it was not, like, a complete hierarchy of dictating what every single agent was doing,” said Ashvin Swaminathan, a member of Axiom’s technical staff. “The agents were finding tasks for themselves and identified things that they could work on in parallel.”

Axiom also trained its own models to be good at math, an approach Hong said most other verification startups haven’t taken. At first, the team relied on one of its in-house Lean experts to teach the agents a human sense of taste. Over time, Hong said, the agents have picked up taste on their own.

The result fills one of the biggest gaps in formalized math. “When you look at what has been formalized in mathematics, there’s this huge black hole. And that black hole covers algebraic geometry,” Swaminathan said.
Until now, researchers who wanted to check new work in algebraic geometry with Lean had little to build on, Swaminathan said. “Well, now they do.”

Axiom argues that each verified result becomes a building block, so future proofs can lean on checked math instead of starting from scratch. Terence Tao, the UCLA mathematician and Fields Medal winner, has made the general case more simply: “The more formalized proofs you have, the more formalized proofs you can make.”

Mathematicians aren’t Axiom’s only intended audience. Developers have long struggled to guarantee that their code is free of bugs and security holes. That problem grows as AI agents write more of the world’s code.
Axiom is betting that the software of the future will need to rest on verified foundations, the way Stacks now does.

“We believe that mathematics is the domain where you start building these things and that it’s a transferable skill,” Swaminathan said. “Agents can read our code, understand it, and build new infrastructure on top of it. Our Lean formalization is now the substrate that agents can build upon.”

The way Axiom’s agents built Stacks, working in parallel and picking their own tasks, is how Hong expects much of AI’s future work to happen. AI agents, she argues, will need a well-built, reusable body of knowledge to keep from producing slop.

“You want [agents] to have a reusable library for them to build on and keep pushing the frontier,” Hong said. “If you slop drop in a way that’s bad engineering choices in the beginning, then it’s very hard for them to grow that boundary.”
Hong is confident enough in that approach to issue a dare. “I openly challenge all the coding companies to work on formalization at this scale.”

感觉人工智能每周都在解决一个新的数学问题。上个月，OpenAI 发布了 719 份手稿，声称可以解决该领域一些最棘手的问题。但即使是旨在确认这些结果的计算机检查也可能会出现失误。经过多年的人工智能衰退，我们有理由怀疑数学是否会成为下一个。
Axiom Math 押注数学可以避免这种命运，不是放慢速度，而是立足更坚定。这家价值 16 亿美元的初创公司希望建立一个经过验证的基础，让人工智能代理可以依赖它来编写软件并最终进行科学研究。
周三，该公司宣布已正式验证 Stacks 项目，这是人类有史以来最大的数学体系之一。数学家们通常很少重视 Stacks——哥伦比亚数学家 Peter Woit 声称“没有其他东西可以真正与之相比”，并将该项目与“著名的 Bourbaki 书籍”进行比较，该系列书籍在 20 世纪重建了数学的基础。
Woit 的哥伦比亚同事 Johan de Jong 于 2005 年启动了 Stacks 项目，作为开源参考。从那时起，数学家们就为它做出了贡献，从大学水平的代数一直到代数、几何和数论领域最先进的思想。
该公司的人工智能代理团队将图书馆的大约 7,654 页翻译成大约 1600 万行计算机检查的代码。
形式化数学是确保其底层结构健全的一种方法。数学家用一种名为 Lean 的编程语言将证明重写为代码，然后由一个名为证明助手的程序逐行检查代码。如果证明通过，数学家就可以相信它在逻辑上是合理的。
工程师使用相同的想法（称为形式验证）来确认他们的芯片设计是否有效，而法国的研究人员则使用它来捕获计算家庭福利的软件中的错误。
对于像 Stacks Project 这样的库，检查每个定理只是工作的一部分。 Stacks 中的定理和定义是相互关联的，每个定理和定义都建立在前一个定理和定义的基础上。就像家谱一样，Stacks 中的许多结果都可以追溯到它之前的结果。
这种相互关联性让 Axiom 不确定该项目一开始是否可行。该团队必须在大约 1600 万行精益代码中保持每个连接完好无损。
Axiom 首席执行官 Carina Hong 向 TechCrunch 表示：“生活中的大事和微妙的事情是不能并存的。” “[Stacks] 是数学结果的集合，是数学的基础。你希望 [定理] 是一致的，而不是自相矛盾的。你希望定义不会相互冲突。”
这位 25 岁的首席执行官从斯坦福大学数学博士项目退学，并于 2025 年 3 月创立了该公司。3 月，Axiom 筹集了由 Menlo Ventures 领投的 2 亿美元 A 轮融资。
“我们不确定氛围编码是否能够保留 Stacks 的美丽，”洪说。
为了完成该项目，该团队为其代理提供了松散的结构，并让他们并行运行。 Axiom 技术人员 Ashvin Swaminathan 表示：“通过 Stacks，我们强加了一个等级制度……但它并不是一个完整的等级制度，规定每个代理的行为。” “代理们正在为自己寻找任务，并确定他们可以并行处理的事情。”
Axiom 还训练了自己的模型，使其擅长数学，洪说，大多数其他验证初创公司都没有采取这种方法。起初，该团队依靠一位内部精益专家来向代理传授人类的味觉。洪说，随着时间的推移，代理商们已经逐渐掌握了自己的品味。
这一结果填补了形式化数学中最大的空白之一。 “当你观察数学中形式化的内容时，就会发现这个巨大的黑洞。这个黑洞涵盖了代数几何，”斯瓦米纳坦说。
斯瓦米纳坦说，到目前为止，想要用 Lean 检查代数几何新工作的研究人员几乎没有什么基础。 “嗯，现在他们做到了。”
Axiom 认为，每个经过验证的结果都会成为一个构建块，因此未来的证明可以依赖于经过检查的数学，而不是从头开始。加州大学洛杉矶分校数学家、菲尔兹奖获得者陶哲轩将一般情况变得更加简单：“你拥有的形式化证明越多，你就能做出越形式化的证明。”
数学家并不是 Axiom 的唯一目标受众。开发人员长期以来一直在努力保证他们的代码没有错误和安全漏洞。随着人工智能代理编写更多的世界代码，这个问题变得越来越严重。
Axiom 认为，未来的软件将需要建立在经过验证的基础上，就像 Stacks 现在所做的那样。
“我们相信数学是你开始构建这些东西的领域，并且它是一种可转移的技能，”斯瓦米纳坦说。 “代理可以阅读我们的代码，理解它，并在其之上构建新的基础设施。我们的精益形式化现在是代理可以构建的基础。”
Axiom 的代理构建 Stacks 的方式是并行工作并选择自己的任务，这是 Hong 预计人工智能未来大部分工作的方式。她认为，人工智能代理需要一个构建良好、可重复使用的知识体系，以防止产生垃圾。
“你希望[代理]拥有一个可重复使用的库，供他们构建并不断推动前沿，”洪说。 “如果一开始就以一种糟糕的工程选择的方式进行下降，那么他们就很难扩大这一边界。”
